newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE white sugar regains some ground as trade buy.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE white sugar regains some ground as trade buy.

text.p: Supportive trade buying dragged nearby white sugar futures back from their earlier lows in solid and mainly outright activity, market sources said on Wednesday.

One leading London commission house accounted for around half of the day's volume, mostly active on the sell side -- but trade players moved in to pick bargains at the lows when spot August sank under $320.
"The trade brought it up from the lows but we've had some fresh spec buying," said one trader. "It was the stops that pulled it down and then the trade came in and pushed it up."
Earlier, August effectively wiped out this month's gains after it gapped lower at the open and then ran into selling from commission houses and European brokers.

August had already weakened on Tuesday as one French brokerage sold the outright position and the nearby spread. Other players took profits as the market fell and took the opportunity to roll spot positions into October.
August opened 80 cents lower on Wednesday at $324.20, still 30 cents below Tuesday's intraday low.
Traders said last week's fund-inspired rally which pushed August to a high of $330.80 was overdone and so the market naturally looked for a downward correction.

At one point, firmness in the New York market sparked August/July arbitrage selling, pushing the differential down to around $71. But then selling on the whites dragged it back out again to $72, traders said.
"The whites got hammered when New York was on a rally," the trader said.
London's August/October spread contracted to around $5.50 after around $8.00/8.50 on Tuesday.
At 1530 GMT August was down $3.20 at a mid-range $321.80 after hitting a session low of $319.70. October was 90 cents lower at $315.80 and volume reached 4,278 lots, the bulk of which was in August.
Traders said they were encouraged by the hefty volume, which they said mostly outright. A small number of against actuals trades were reported, along with options interest in December $310 puts.
Paris followed a similar pattern to London with all traded positions weaker on the day.
August was down $2.50 at $321.50 and October down $1.00 at $315.50. Matif volume totalled 563 lots.
